reading.body:
AI litigation in United States courts is tracked as living case pages refreshed daily from CourtListener, but this hub carries no case count of its own.

The structure is two parts. One is the docket tracker, which follows active AI lawsuits as they move. The other is the precedent set, the older decisions that current AI copyright, scraping and defamation cases are argued out of: Sony on substantial non-infringing use, Campbell and Google Books on transformative purpose, Van Buren and hiQ on scraping, Zeran on Section 230.

That second part is the useful signal. Every one of those precedents was decided long before generative models existed. The legal questions AI companies face are being resolved by courts that never saw the technology, which means outcomes turn on analogy rather than on rules written for AI.

What this does not cover is scale. The total is zero and the points list is empty, so nothing here says how many suits are pending, which districts they sit in, or how any of them have been decided. The refresh cadence is seven days, so the tracker is current to within a week, not to the minute.
